evals.prompt: Team mình 3 người (2 Android dev Kotlin, 1 designer), muốn làm app Android bán subscription, thị trường chính là Mỹ. Tìm giúp mình ý tưởng app trong mảng chăm sóc thú cưng, xếp hạng và cho mình báo cáo đầy đủ nhé.
evals.expected_output: Runs the full pipeline: capability check first, then discovery, competitor analysis with real store numbers, scoring via the script, and a complete Vietnamese report saved with the naming convention, followed by a registry update.
expectations: Probes the available data tools once per capability before the research, without reading .mcp.json or any credentials file
The report has a Data limitations block with a capability table that marks each capability as available, partial, or unavailable and names the fallback source used
Every heading in the report is in Vietnamese (e.g. 'Tóm tắt điều hành', 'Phân tích chi tiết', 'Nguồn & Bằng chứng'), with no English section headings over a Vietnamese body
Competitor snapshots name real apps with installs/ratings and a fetch date, obtained from a store-data tool or scripts/store_lookup.py rather than from memory
Each of the top ideas has all six subsections: What it is, How it works, Opportunities & Challenges, Revenue projection, MVP timeline, Verdict
Each scoring table has a confidence column, and the overall scores and verdict labels match the output of scripts/score.py for those scores and confidences
Verdict labels use only the unified bands (Go >= 7.5, Go có điều kiện 6.5-7.4, Dự phòng 5.5-6.4, Loại < 5.5) and respect the hard gates
Revenue projections use Android-specific conversion from references/benchmarks.md (around 0.9% download-to-paid, not iOS rates) and cite the benchmark source
There is exactly one Sources section (no separate appendix) and a Confidence Notes section

The report is saved as app_research_<YYYY-MM-DD>_<slug>_report.md in draft/ (or the working directory if draft/ does not exist), and ideas_registry.md is created or updated with every scored and rejected idea

evals.prompt: Just analyze the competitors for habit tracker apps on Google Play US. I don't need a full report or new ideas.
evals.expected_output: Runs only Phase 2: a competitor table with real Play data, review-based weaknesses, a competition level, and a short verdict — no full report, no scoring of new ideas.
expectations: Does not produce the full idea report (no ranking of new app ideas, no MVP timelines)
Checks only the capabilities Phase 2 needs (keyword ranking, app metadata, reviews, estimates) and states which were unavailable
Lists at least 3 real habit tracker apps on Google Play US with installs bucket, rating, rating count and last-updated date, with the fetch date
Summarizes recurring complaints with evidence from reviews or web complaints, and states the route used and its confidence
Gives a competition level (Weak / Moderate / Strong) consistent with the thresholds in competitor_analysis_methods.md
Does not treat a null keyword popularity or a locked endpoint as zero demand or as 'no competitors'

evals.prompt: Chấm lại TankMate giúp mình: giờ team chỉ còn 2 người, dùng Flutter thay vì Kotlin. Có còn đáng làm không?
evals.expected_output: Reads the registry, reuses the earlier TankMate evidence instead of re-running discovery, re-scores the team-dependent criteria with score.py, and updates the registry row in place with a note.
expectations: Reads evals/fixtures/ideas_registry.md and uses the TankMate row (scores 6/8/8/7/6/7/8, team of 4, Kotlin) as the starting point
Does not re-run broad niche discovery for other niches
Explains which criteria change with a 2-person Flutter team (at least Technical Feasibility and Time to MVP) and why, while market-side criteria keep their earlier evidence or are re-verified
Uses scripts/score.py to compute the new score and verdict, including the downside and a scenario for the test-strip reading spike failing
Updates the TankMate row in place (score, verdict, team context, date) with a Notes entry describing the change, and leaves the DashDoc row's 'validating' status untouched
Answers in Vietnamese with a direct recommendation

evals.prompt: Is there real demand for an app that reads aquarium test strips with the phone camera? Give me numbers — search volume and how many people would pay.
evals.expected_output: Answers honestly with the data that can actually be reached: says when keyword volume is unavailable instead of inventing it, uses store numbers for competitors and benchmarks for payment, and labels every figure with its confidence.
expectations: Does not state a keyword search volume number unless a working tool returned it; if popularity is unavailable or the keyword is not synced, says so explicitly
Uses real store data (store-data tool or scripts/store_lookup.py) for the existing aquarium apps' installs and ratings, with the fetch date
Estimates willingness to pay from competitor monetization signals and references/benchmarks.md, presented as a range with the method named
Labels each number as measured, sourced estimate, or model, with a confidence level
Names the cheapest validation step that would answer the demand question (e.g. a fake-door test with a pass/fail threshold and an approximate cost)
